entries.title: The 1996-2002 telecom fiber overbuild

facts.text: The Federal Reserve Bank of Richmond reported that U.S. investment in communications equipment grew from approximately $62 billion per year in the first quarter of 1996 to over $135 billion per year in the fourth quarter of 2000, in constant 1996 dollars.

source.title: Boom and Bust in Telecommunications, Economic Quarterly Volume 89/4 (Fall 2003)

facts.text: The same article reported that communications equipment investment fell to under $93 billion in the fourth quarter of 2001, only 69 percent of the level one year earlier.

source.title: Boom and Bust in Telecommunications, Economic Quarterly Volume 89/4 (Fall 2003)

facts.text: The article stated that by early 2001 it had become apparent that massive overinvestment had taken place in the telecommunications sector, particularly in long-distance fiber-optic cable.

source.title: Boom and Bust in Telecommunications, Economic Quarterly Volume 89/4 (Fall 2003)

facts.text: The article reported that consumption of telecommunications services grew steadily from approximately $88 billion in 1995 to $151 billion in 2001, in constant 1996 dollars.

source.title: Boom and Bust in Telecommunications, Economic Quarterly Volume 89/4 (Fall 2003)

facts.text: The article reported that telecommunications industry employment peaked at approximately 1.59 million workers in March 2001 and declined 22 percent to about 1.30 million by July 2003.

source.title: Boom and Bust in Telecommunications, Economic Quarterly Volume 89/4 (Fall 2003)

facts.text: The Federal Reserve Bank of San Francisco reported that capital investment by publicly traded telecom service companies rose from $47 billion in 1995 to a peak of $121 billion in 2000 and fell to $49 billion by 2002.

source.title: The Boom and Bust in Information Technology Investment, FRBSF Economic Review 2004
source.publisher: Federal Reserve Bank of San Francisco

facts.text: A Federal Reserve Board working paper stated that more than 90 percent of the optical fiber cables installed during the 1990s were left unused in the years that followed.

source.title: Learning By Investing: Embodied Technology and Business Cycles (Finance and Economics Discussion Series 2007-15)
source.publisher: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System

facts.text: The same paper noted that this level of unused fiber was also partly due to a new signal transmitting technology that dramatically increased the transmitting capacity of each cable.

source.title: Learning By Investing: Embodied Technology and Business Cycles (Finance and Economics Discussion Series 2007-15)
source.publisher: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System

facts.text: A 2003 academic paper from the University of Minnesota estimated that U.S. Internet traffic had approximately doubled every year since 1997, and described 1995 and 1996 as an anomalous two-year period when traffic grew at about the rate of a doubling every 100 days.

facts.text: A 2026 Federal Reserve Board staff note, using Bureau of Economic Analysis data, reported that the U.S. intellectual property and equipment investment share of GDP reached 11.5 percent in 2000 and that as of the first quarter of 2026 it was about 0.8 percentage points above its 2024 level and slightly below the 2000 peak.

source.title: Do Major Technology Advancements Lead to Overinvestment? (FEDS Notes)

entries.title: GE Vernova: power generation and grid equipment

facts.text: On April 2, 2024, General Electric Company, which now operates as GE Aerospace, completed the spin-off of GE Vernova by distributing all of GE Vernova's common stock to GE's stockholders, and GE Vernova became an independent company.

source.title: GE Vernova Inc. Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended December 31, 2025

facts.text: GE Vernova is a Delaware corporation with corporate headquarters in Cambridge, Massachusetts, and it reports three business segments: Power, Wind and Electrification.

source.title: GE Vernova Inc. Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended December 31, 2025

facts.text: GE Vernova's Power segment products include gas and steam turbines, full balance of plant, upgrade and service solutions, and its Gas Power business offers heavy-duty and aeroderivative gas turbines for utilities, independent power producers and industrial applications.

source.title: GE Vernova Inc. Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended December 31, 2025

facts.text: GE Vernova's Electrification segment provides products and services for the transmission, distribution, conversion, storage and orchestration of electricity, with offerings that include high-voltage direct current transmission, alternating current substation solutions, power transformers, switchgear and synchronous condensers.

source.title: GE Vernova Inc. Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended December 31, 2025

facts.text: GE Vernova's total revenues were $38,068 million in 2025, compared with $34,935 million in 2024 and $33,239 million in 2023; 2025 revenues comprised $20,934 million of equipment revenues and $17,134 million of services revenues.

source.title: GE Vernova Inc. Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended December 31, 2025

facts.text: In 2025, GE Vernova's Power segment had revenues of $19,767 million, its Wind segment $9,110 million and its Electrification segment $9,642 million.

source.title: GE Vernova Inc. Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended December 31, 2025

facts.text: GE Vernova's segment EBITDA for 2025 was $2,902 million for Power, $1,433 million for Electrification and negative $598 million for Wind.

source.title: GE Vernova Inc. Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended December 31, 2025

facts.text: GE Vernova reported remaining performance obligations (RPO), a measure of backlog that includes unfilled firm and unconditional customer orders for equipment and services, excluding any purchase order the customer can cancel or terminate without a substantive penalty, of $150.2 billion at December 31, 2025, compared with $119.0 billion at December 31, 2024.

source.title: GE Vernova Inc. Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended December 31, 2025

facts.text: As of December 31, 2025, GE Vernova had a gas turbine installed base of approximately 7,000 units, with approximately 1,800 units under long-term service agreements with an average remaining contract life of approximately 10 years.

source.title: GE Vernova Inc. Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended December 31, 2025

facts.text: GE Vernova's 10-K states that, in its Electrification segment, demand remains strong for large-scale transmission-related equipment to interconnect renewables and move bulk power, and that it also continues to benefit from higher growth in orders from other transmission activities to connect new power sources, to electrify industries including data centers, and to modernize existing grid infrastructure.

source.title: GE Vernova Inc. Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended December 31, 2025

facts.text: GE Vernova's 10-K states that its installed base generates approximately 25% of the world's electricity.

entries.title: Dominion Energy: a regulated utility serving data centres

facts.text: Dominion Energy manages its daily operations through three primary operating segments, Dominion Energy Virginia, Dominion Energy South Carolina and Contracted Energy, and it also reports a Corporate and Other segment.

source.title: Dominion Energy, Inc. Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended December 31, 2025 (combined filing with Virginia Electric and Power Company)

facts.text: Dominion Energy Virginia is composed of Virginia Power's regulated electric transmission, distribution and generation operations, which serve approximately 2.8 million residential, commercial, high load (including certain data centers), industrial and governmental customers in Virginia and North Carolina.

source.title: Dominion Energy, Inc. Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended December 31, 2025 (combined filing with Virginia Electric and Power Company)

facts.text: Data centers represented 28% of Virginia Power's electricity sales in 2025 and 26% in 2024.

source.title: Dominion Energy, Inc. Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended December 31, 2025 (combined filing with Virginia Electric and Power Company)

facts.text: Dominion's 10-K states that the concentration of data centers primarily in Loudoun County, Virginia requires significant investments in electric transmission and generation facilities to meet the growing demand.

source.title: Dominion Energy, Inc. Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended December 31, 2025 (combined filing with Virginia Electric and Power Company)

facts.text: Virginia Power recorded regulated electric sales revenue of $1,811 million in 2025, $1,362 million in 2024 and $1,308 million in 2023 from high load customers, which the 10-K defines as customers in Virginia, including certain data centers, with actual or anticipated forecast demand of 25 MW or higher and an annual load factor of 75% or higher.

source.title: Dominion Energy, Inc. Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended December 31, 2025 (combined filing with Virginia Electric and Power Company)

facts.text: Dominion Energy's total operating revenue was $16,506 million in 2025 and $14,459 million in 2024; Virginia Power's total operating revenue was $11,812 million in 2025 and $10,235 million in 2024.

source.title: Dominion Energy, Inc. Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended December 31, 2025 (combined filing with Virginia Electric and Power Company)

facts.text: Virginia's Regulation Act provides for a cost-of-service rate model, and the Virginia Commission reviews Virginia Power's retail base rates for generation and distribution services to customers in Virginia in a biennial proceeding that determines its actual earned return on equity (ROE) during a historic test period and its authorized ROE prospectively.

source.title: Dominion Energy, Inc. Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended December 31, 2025 (combined filing with Virginia Electric and Power Company)

facts.text: In November 2025, the Virginia Commission approved a Virginia Power base rate increase of $566 million effective January 2026, with an incremental base rate increase of $210 million effective January 2027, and authorized an ROE of 9.80% for Virginia Power.

source.title: Dominion Energy, Inc. Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended December 31, 2025 (combined filing with Virginia Electric and Power Company)

facts.text: Virginia Power requires deposits for expensive long lead-time equipment along with reimbursement clauses for canceled projects, and under the terms of the 2025 Biennial Review order it will begin in January 2027 to require a 14-year contract, collateral over that period and demand minimums for distribution, transmission and generation revenues for high load customers at connection.

source.title: Dominion Energy, Inc. Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended December 31, 2025 (combined filing with Virginia Electric and Power Company)

facts.text: At December 31, 2025, Dominion Energy had approximately 15,200 full-time employees, including approximately 6,700 at Virginia Power.

source.title: Dominion Energy, Inc. Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended December 31, 2025 (combined filing with Virginia Electric and Power Company)

entries.title: BlackBerry's smartphone decline, 2011-2017

companies.name: BlackBerry Limited (formerly Research In Motion Limited)

facts.text: Research In Motion (RIM), the maker of BlackBerry smartphones, reported revenue of $19.9 billion and net income of $3.4 billion for its fiscal year 2011, which ended February 26, 2011.

source.title: Research In Motion Limited Management's Discussion and Analysis for the fiscal year ended March 3, 2012 (Form 40-F, Exhibit 1.3)

facts.text: For fiscal 2012, RIM's revenue fell 7.4% to $18.4 billion, the number of BlackBerry devices sold decreased 6.3%, or approximately 3.3 million, to approximately 49.0 million from approximately 52.3 million, and net income fell 64.7% to $1.2 billion.

source.title: Research In Motion Limited Management's Discussion and Analysis for the fiscal year ended March 3, 2012 (Form 40-F, Exhibit 1.3)

facts.text: On January 30, 2013, Research In Motion announced that it would operate around the world under the name BlackBerry, effective immediately, adopting the name of its BlackBerry smartphone to coincide with the launch of its new BlackBerry 10 platform.

source.title: Research In Motion Form 6-K: Research In Motion Changes Its Name to BlackBerry (news release of January 30, 2013)

facts.text: BlackBerry's fiscal 2014 MD&A states that sell-through of BlackBerry 10 smartphones decreased significantly during the year due to the maturing smartphone market, very intense competition and, in the company's view, uncertainty created by its strategic review process, leaving more BlackBerry 10 devices in the sales channel than it expected.

source.title: BlackBerry Limited Management's Discussion and Analysis for the fiscal year ended March 1, 2014 (Form 40-F, Exhibit 1.3)

facts.text: BlackBerry recorded primarily non-cash, pre-tax charges against inventory and supply commitments of approximately $934 million in the second quarter of fiscal 2014, primarily attributable to BlackBerry Z10 devices, and approximately $1.6 billion in the third quarter, primarily attributable to BlackBerry 10 devices, and it canceled plans to launch two devices.

source.title: BlackBerry Limited Management's Discussion and Analysis for the fiscal year ended March 1, 2014 (Form 40-F, Exhibit 1.3)

facts.text: In September 2013, BlackBerry announced restructuring plans that included a reduction of approximately 4,500 employees, said it would refocus on the enterprise and prosumer market, and said its future smartphone portfolio would go from six devices to four.

source.title: BlackBerry Limited Form 6-K: BlackBerry Announces Preliminary Second Quarter Fiscal 2014 Results and Provides Business Update (news release of September 20, 2013)

facts.text: BlackBerry's revenue from continuing operations for fiscal 2014 was $6.8 billion, a decrease of 38.5%, or approximately $4.3 billion, from $11.1 billion in fiscal 2013; hardware revenue fell 43.1% to $3.8 billion, and the net loss from continuing operations was $5.9 billion.

source.title: BlackBerry Limited Management's Discussion and Analysis for the fiscal year ended March 1, 2014 (Form 40-F, Exhibit 1.3)

facts.text: BlackBerry's fiscal 2014 MD&A states that many IT departments that had required employees to use the BlackBerry wireless solution were permitting them to choose competitors' devices (the bring-your-own-device trend), which affected its enterprise subscriber account base.

source.title: BlackBerry Limited Management's Discussion and Analysis for the fiscal year ended March 1, 2014 (Form 40-F, Exhibit 1.3)

facts.text: The same MD&A states that BlackBerry earned service revenue mainly from a monthly service access fee charged to carriers or resellers for subscribers on BlackBerry 7 and earlier operating systems, that many competitors did not charge such a fee, and that it faced significant pressure to reduce the fee, especially for consumers.

source.title: BlackBerry Limited Management's Discussion and Analysis for the fiscal year ended March 1, 2014 (Form 40-F, Exhibit 1.3)

facts.text: By fiscal 2017 BlackBerry described itself as a mobile-native security software and services company. Its Mobility Solutions segment included the development and licensing of its secure device software and the outsourcing to partners of all design, manufacturing, sales and customer support for BlackBerry-branded handsets, as well as sales of its existing DTEK60, DTEK50, Priv, Leap and Passport smartphones.

source.title: BlackBerry Limited Management's Discussion and Analysis for the fiscal year ended February 28, 2017 (Form 40-F, Exhibit 1.3)

facts.text: BlackBerry's consolidated revenue fell by $851 million to approximately $1.3 billion in fiscal 2017 from $2.2 billion in fiscal 2016, including a $510 million decrease in hardware and other revenues to $374 million and a $466 million decrease in service access fee revenues to $313 million.

source.title: BlackBerry Limited Management's Discussion and Analysis for the fiscal year ended February 28, 2017 (Form 40-F, Exhibit 1.3)

entries.title: Blockbuster's decline and sale, 2003-2013

facts.text: Blockbuster's 10-K for 2004 described it as a leading global provider of in-home rental and retail movie and game entertainment, with approximately 9,100 stores in the United States, its territories and 24 other countries as of December 31, 2004, and total revenues of $6.1 billion for 2004.

source.title: Blockbuster Inc. Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended December 31, 2004

facts.text: During 2004 Blockbuster launched BLOCKBUSTER ONLINE, its U.S. online subscription program, and its 10-K described its rental business as mature and as having continued to decline during 2004.

source.title: Blockbuster Inc. Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended December 31, 2004

facts.text: In December 2004 Blockbuster announced the end of late fees beginning on January 1, 2005, meaning it no longer charged extended viewing fees on any movie or game rental at more than 4,500 company-operated stores and approximately 550 participating franchise stores in the United States.

source.title: Blockbuster Inc. Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended December 31, 2004

facts.text: Blockbuster recorded goodwill impairment charges of $1.29 billion in the fourth quarter of 2003 and $1.50 billion in the third quarter of 2004; for the 2004 charge its 10-K cited the accelerated decline in the in-store rental industry, accelerated investments in new initiatives and other growth opportunities, and increased competition in the online movie rental industry.

source.title: Blockbuster Inc. Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended December 31, 2004

facts.text: On September 3, 2004, before Viacom completed its divestiture of Blockbuster, Blockbuster paid a special distribution of approximately $905.6 million, or $5 per share, to its stockholders including Viacom; to fund it, Blockbuster entered into a $1,150.0 million senior secured credit facility and issued $300.0 million of 9% senior subordinated notes.

source.title: Blockbuster Inc. Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended December 31, 2004

facts.text: Blockbuster's revenues were $4,062.4 million for fiscal 2009, compared with $5,065.4 million for fiscal 2008, and it reported a net loss of $558.2 million for fiscal 2009 that included $369.2 million of non-cash impairment charges to goodwill and other long-lived assets.

source.title: Blockbuster Inc. Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended January 3, 2010

facts.text: As of January 3, 2010, Blockbuster had over 6,500 stores in the United States, its territories and 17 other countries.

source.title: Blockbuster Inc. Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended January 3, 2010

facts.text: In fiscal 2009 Blockbuster's domestic segment revenues decreased 20.4% and its domestic same-store revenues decreased 15.6%; the company said it believed the declines were caused primarily by increased competition from retail mass merchant sales of low-priced DVDs, by-mail rentals, kiosk and vending rental and sales and other sources of in-home entertainment, by competition from other forms of leisure entertainment, and by sustained decreases in consumer spending attributable to the decline in overall economic conditions.

source.title: Blockbuster Inc. Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended January 3, 2010

facts.text: Blockbuster's fiscal 2009 10-K stated that its net loss from operations, its stockholders' deficit and increasingly competitive industry conditions raised substantial doubt about its ability to continue as a going concern.

source.title: Blockbuster Inc. Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended January 3, 2010

facts.text: On September 23, 2010, Blockbuster and certain of its domestic subsidiaries filed voluntary petitions under Chapter 11 of the U.S. Bankruptcy Code, and after an auction on April 6, 2011 it selected DISH Network Corporation's bid as the highest and best, under which DISH agreed to buy substantially all of its assets for approximately $320 million, subject to adjustments.

source.title: Blockbuster Inc. Form 8-K reporting the April 6, 2011 asset sale agreement with DISH Network

facts.text: The sale of substantially all of Blockbuster's assets to DISH closed on April 26, 2011.

source.title: Blockbuster Inc. Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended January 2, 2011

facts.text: DISH's 10-K for 2013 states that on November 6, 2013 it announced that Blockbuster would close all of its remaining company-owned domestic retail stores and discontinue the Blockbuster by-mail DVD service, and that as of December 31, 2013 Blockbuster had ceased all material operations.

entries.title: Nokia's handset business, 2010-2016

facts.text: Nokia's Devices & Services net sales were EUR 29,134 million in 2010, EUR 23,943 million in 2011 (down 18%) and EUR 15,686 million in 2012 (down 34%).

source.title: Nokia Corporation Form 20-F for the fiscal year ended December 31, 2012

facts.text: Nokia's Devices & Services operating profit fell 75% to EUR 884 million in 2011 from EUR 3,540 million in 2010, and the business reported an operating loss of EUR 1,100 million in 2012; its operating margin went from 12.2% in 2010 to 3.7% in 2011 and negative 7.0% in 2012.

source.title: Nokia Corporation Form 20-F for the fiscal year ended December 31, 2012

facts.text: On February 11, 2011, Nokia and Microsoft announced plans for a broad strategic partnership under which Nokia would adopt Windows Phone as its principal smartphone strategy.

source.title: Nokia Corporation Form 6-K: stock exchange releases of February 11, 2011

facts.text: A Nokia strategy release of the same day stated that, with the planned move to Windows Phone as its primary smartphone platform, Symbian would become a franchise platform.

source.title: Nokia Corporation Form 6-K: stock exchange releases of February 11, 2011

facts.text: Nokia's Smart Devices volume decreased 55% to 35.1 million units in 2012 from 77.3 million units in 2011, a decrease its 20-F attributed to the strong momentum of competing smartphone platforms relative to its Symbian devices.

source.title: Nokia Corporation Form 20-F for the fiscal year ended December 31, 2012

facts.text: Nokia's Smart Devices business shipped a total of 13.4 million Lumia devices in 2012.

source.title: Nokia Corporation Form 20-F for the fiscal year ended December 31, 2012

facts.text: On September 3, 2013, Nokia announced an agreement to sell substantially all of its Devices & Services business and license its patents to Microsoft for EUR 5.44 billion in cash, of which EUR 3.79 billion related to the business and EUR 1.65 billion to the mutual patent agreement and future option.

source.title: Nokia Corporation Form 6-K: Nokia to sell Devices & Services business to Microsoft (stock exchange releases of September 3, 2013)

facts.text: A joint Microsoft and Nokia announcement filed by Nokia stated that the operations planned to be transferred to Microsoft generated an estimated EUR 14.9 billion, almost 50 percent of Nokia's net sales for 2012, and that approximately 32,000 people were expected to transfer at closing.

source.title: Nokia Corporation Form 6-K: Nokia to sell Devices & Services business to Microsoft (stock exchange releases of September 3, 2013)

facts.text: Nokia completed the sale of substantially all of its Devices & Services business to Microsoft on April 25, 2014.

source.title: Nokia Corporation Form 6-K: Nokia completes sale of substantially all of its Devices & Services business to Microsoft (stock exchange release of April 25, 2014)

facts.text: Microsoft's 10-K for fiscal 2015 reports that on April 25, 2014 it acquired substantially all of Nokia's Devices and Services business for a total purchase price of $9.4 billion, including cash acquired of $1.5 billion, and that in the fourth quarter of fiscal 2015 it recorded a $5.1 billion goodwill impairment charge, reducing Phone Hardware's goodwill from $5.4 billion to $116 million, net of foreign currency remeasurements, as well as a $2.2 billion impairment charge related to the write-down of Phone Hardware intangible assets.

source.title: Microsoft Corporation Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended June 30, 2015

facts.text: Microsoft's 10-K for fiscal 2016 states that a restructuring plan approved in June 2015 eliminated approximately 7,400 positions in fiscal 2016, primarily in its phone hardware business, and that in May 2016 it announced plans to further streamline its smartphone hardware business and the sale of its entry-level feature phone business for $350 million.
